mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B's recent shots FOR (18.2) substantially exceeds its all-prior average (14.8) while Team B's shots-on-target FOR in recent form (7.0) is also elevated, AND simultaneously Team A's shots AGAINST in recent form (16.6) exceeds its all-prior average (13.6). Measure whether the combination of high opponent shot volume AND high shots-on-target allowed (Team A recent: 7.2 vs all-prior 5.1) co-occurs with elevated goals-against rates beyond what either observable predicts individually.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both shot volume and shots-on-target allowed are jointly elevated for the defending team, goals conceded rises more than when only one of the two observables is elevated — a super-additive joint relationship.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot volume (shots FOR) is jointly elevated in recent form alongside a divergence between shots and shots-on-target FOR, suggesting a conversion-efficiency gap that interacts with Team A's recent defensive deterioration (shots AGAINST rising sharply in recent 5 vs all-prior). The joint pattern of high shot volume but low conversion rate for one side meeting a leaky defensive shape for the other is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires the joint conditioning of two distinct observables (shots and shots-on-target) for two different sides simultaneously; it cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where the away team (Team B) has a large home-vs-away gap in shots FOR and shots-on-target FOR, AND the home team (Team A) shows a recent-vs-all-prior decline in shots-on-target FOR. Measure whether the net shots-on-target differential between the two teams in this joint configuration differs from what each team's individual venue split or recent trend would predict independently.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The net shots-on-target balance favours the home team less (or reverses) when the away team's venue penalty is large and the home team's attacking output is simultaneously in recent decline — the two dimensions interact to suppress the home attacking advantage.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B exhibits an asymmetric home/away split in shots FOR (home: 16.84, away: 12.57) and shots-on-target FOR (home: 5.72, away: 4.17), while simultaneously Team A's shots-on-target FOR is declining in recent form (3.6 recent vs 4.67 all-prior). The cross-team asymmetry — one team's attacking output being venue-dependent while the other's attacking output is deteriorating — jointly shapes the expected shot-on-target balance in a way neither team's single-observable venue split captures alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires simultaneously conditioning on two distinct observables (shots and shots-on-target) across two different teams with different directional signals; not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where the away team's recent foul rate FOR is elevated above its all-prior average AND the home team's recent yellow cards AGAINST is elevated above its all-prior average. Measure whether cards_2h in the second half is higher in this joint configuration than when only one of the two conditions holds.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half card volume rises when both the away team's foul rate and the home team's cards-against rate are jointly elevated, more so than when either condition holds in isolation.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's foul rate has surged in recent form (14.8 recent vs 12.1 all-prior FOR fouls) while Team A's yellow cards AGAINST have also risen in recent form (2.4 recent vs 1.74 all-prior). The joint elevation of opponent foul production and cards-against for the home team — two distinct observables — suggests a disciplinary interaction: when the away team commits more fouls AND the home team is conceding more cards, the second-half card volume (cards_2h) may be jointly elevated beyond what either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires joint conditioning on two distinct observables (fouls FOR for one team, yellow_cards AGAINST for the other) across two teams; not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where a team's fouls FOR and yellow_cards FOR are both rising in recent form relative to all-prior, while yellow_cards AGAINST is simultaneously falling. Measure whether the fouls-to-yellow-card conversion rate (fouls per yellow card) for the team's opponents is non-linearly suppressed in this configuration, indicating a threshold or saturation effect in how foul volume translates to cards.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's own foul rate and self-received card rate are both rising while opponent card rate is falling, the fouls-to-cards conversion rate for opponents saturates or decouples — the relationship between fouls and cards is non-linear and direction-asymmetric.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's yellow cards FOR in recent form (2.4) have risen above its all-prior average (1.75) while its fouls FOR have also surged (14.8 recent vs 12.1 all-prior), but Team B's yellow cards AGAINST have dropped sharply in recent form (0.8 recent vs 1.73 all-prior). This creates an asymmetric disciplinary profile: Team B is committing more fouls and receiving more cards itself, while its opponents are receiving fewer cards against it. The ratio of fouls-to-cards (a non-linear conversion rate) differs across the two directions and across recent vs all-prior windows simultaneously.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly tracking two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) in two directions (FOR and AGAINST) for the same team, with a non-linear ratio relationship; not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where both teams are in below-average possession FOR in recent form (both below 50%), and simultaneously the team with the lower possession is the home team. Measure whether corner kicks FOR for the home team are suppressed relative to its home-venue all-prior average when possession is jointly low for both sides, testing whether corner kick generation has a threshold dependence on possession share rather than a linear one.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Corner kick generation for the home team is suppressed below its home-venue baseline when both teams are simultaneously in low-possession regimes, suggesting a threshold or saturation in the possession-to-corners relationship rather than a proportional one.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession FOR is declining in recent form (46.0 recent vs 48.5 all-prior) while Team B's possession AGAINST is also declining (44.6 recent vs 48.7 all-prior FOR, with opponent possession rising to 55.4 recent vs 51.3 all-prior AGAINST). Simultaneously, Team A's corner kicks FOR show a home/away split (home: 5.68, away: 4.78) and Team B's corner kicks AGAINST have risen in recent form (6.6 recent vs 5.83 all-prior). The joint relationship between possession balance and corner kick generation — two distinct observables — may reveal whether possession dominance translates to corner kick volume in a non-proportional (threshold) way when both teams are in low-possession regimes.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) across both teams simultaneously, with a threshold/non-linear dependence tested; not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.
